medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning

reports.text: Specimen: pericardium, radical pericardiectomy. Gross: multiple fragments of tan-white, firm pericardial tissue up to 7 cm, with gritty calcified areas. Microscopic: dense hyalinized fibrous tissue with dystrophic calcification and sparse chronic inflammation. No granulomas. No malignancy identified.
reports.conclusion: Fibrotic, calcified pericardium consistent with constrictive pericarditis. Negative for malignancy.

documents.title: Discharge summary, cardiac surgery (outside)
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
Regional medical center, cardiac surgery service.
Admitted 01/16/2024. Discharged 01/23/2024.
Patient: Howard Nadeau, 58 y/o M.
Allergies: penicillin (rash); shellfish (anaphylaxis).

Diagnosis: constrictive pericarditis, radiation-associated (mantle field radiation 2003), confirmed by MRI and catheterization.

Procedure 01/16/2024: radical pericardiectomy via median sternotomy, phrenic nerve to phrenic nerve, without cardiopulmonary bypass. Thick calcified pericardium removed; immediate improvement in RV filling on TEE.
Pathology: fibrotic calcified pericardium, no malignancy.

Course: extubated the evening of surgery. Chest tubes out day 3. Brief diuresis IV, transitioned back to oral. Atrial rhythm sinus throughout. Walking the halls by day 4. Pain controlled with acetaminophen. Aspirin resumed day 2.

Discharge medications: furosemide 20 mg daily (reduced from 40), amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, calcium carbonate/vitamin D twice daily, leuprolide per urology schedule.
Sternal precautions 6 weeks, no driving 4 weeks. Follow up with cardiology in about 3 months and PCP in 1-2 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks out from pericardiectomy (1/16, discharged 1/23). Discharge summary arrived 1/30 and reviewed.

He says the stairs are already easier than before surgery. Sternum sore when he coughs or rolls over, uses acetaminophen at night. Sleeping in a recliner the first week, now in bed. Appetite fine. Ankles mostly down. Taking furosemide 20 each morning.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, weight 84 kg, down 6 kg from September. Sternal incision healing well, no drainage or erythema, sternum stable. JVP not elevated. Heart regular, no rub. Lungs clear. Abdomen flat, no fluid wave. Trace ankle edema.

A/P
1. S/p radical pericardiectomy for radiation-associated constriction, recovering well. BMP and CBC today. Furosemide per cardiology, follow-up there in April.
2. HTN: BP fine on amlodipine plus the diuretic.
3. Return to desk work after cardiology clears; sternal precautions until early March.
Short-term leave paperwork completed for his employer.

documents.title: Refill amlodipine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can you send a new amlodipine script to the mail order pharmacy? My insurance switched me to 90 days by mail. Back at work this week, feeling good.

documents.title: RE: Refill amlodipine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Sent amlodipine 5 mg, 90 days with refills, to the mail order pharmacy on file. Glad you're back at it.

documents.title: Urology follow-up letter
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group, office visit 04/09/2024.
Re: Howard Nadeau.
He had a pericardiectomy in January and is recovering. Leuprolide 7.5 mg IM every 28 days was given on schedule around the surgery.
Allergies: penicillin (rash), shellfish (anaphylaxis).
PSA 0.2 ng/mL, now low but detectable after prior undetectable values.
Plan: continue leuprolide. Repeat PSA in 3 months; if rising, consider imaging.
Outside urology

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Visit 04/18/2024.
Mr. Nadeau returns three months after radical pericardiectomy for radiation-associated constriction. He climbs two flights at work without stopping, no orthopnea, no swelling for the past month. Taking furosemide 20 mg daily.
Meds: furosemide 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg, aspirin 81 mg, calcium/vitamin D, leuprolide (urology).
Allergies: penicillin (rash), shellfish (anaphylaxis).
Exam: vitals as recorded. JVP normal. No knock. Sternotomy healed. Abdomen without ascites, liver not palpable. No edema.
Labs: BNP 62. ALT, AST, bilirubin and albumin normal.
Impression: constrictive pericarditis resolved after pericardiectomy, congestion cleared.
Plan: stop furosemide. Weigh weekly; call if more than 2 kg up or swelling returns. Echo and visit in one year, sooner if symptoms.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual visit.

Interval: pericardiectomy in January; cardiology took him off furosemide in April and he's had no swelling since. Walking 30 minutes most evenings. Urology letter from April: PSA 0.2, repeat planned in 3 months there. Still on leuprolide.
Meds: amlodipine 5, atorvastatin 20, aspirin 81, calcium/D twice daily, leuprolide via urology; epi pen at home.
Allergies: penicillin, shellfish.
No smoking. PHQ-9 2.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well. Sternotomy scar healed. Heart regular, no rub or knock. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly or fluid. No edema. Skin: no lesions of concern in the old radiation field.

A/P
1. S/p pericardiectomy, doing well.
2. HTN controlled on amlodipine alone.
3. Lipids, CMP, CBC, TSH, vitamin D today.
4. Osteopenia on ADT: due for DXA, ordered.
5. Tdap today (last one he can't recall). Lung CT due August, ordered.
6. Prostate cancer per urology.

documents.title: Bone density and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Howard, the bone density scan still shows osteopenia (thinner than average bone, not osteoporosis). The hip number slipped a little since 2022, which is expected on leuprolide. Keep up the calcium/vitamin D and walking. Your June labs were all fine, including vitamin D. We'll recheck the scan in two years.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
Low-dose CT chest without contrast. Comparison 7/11/2023.
Lungs: no nodules. No consolidation.
Pleura: no effusion.
Heart and mediastinum: interval median sternotomy and pericardiectomy; small residual pericardial calcification posteriorly. Heart size normal. No effusion. No adenopathy.
Upper abdomen: postsplenectomy.
Bones: sternotomy wires intact. No suspicious osseous lesion.

documents.body: Negative screen, Lung-RADS 1; post-surgical change only. Next in a year.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six-month check. Feels well, back to full days at work, walking most evenings. No swelling, no breathlessness. No urology letter here since April; he isn't sure whether the 3-month PSA recheck got done. Asked him to have urology send their notes. Due back to cardiology in January.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
- HTN at goal on amlodipine 5.
- Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 20, June LDL acceptable.
- Prostate cancer per urology.
- Physical in June.
